beats.text: Green acid ponds and yellow crust, with a pH below one.
How does a desert end up full of acid?
The Afar people called it Dallol, which means disintegration.
Its mountain stands about as tall as a twenty-storey building.
A round hollow in the middle is probably a collapsed crater.
The mountain is a cinder cone volcano feeding hot springs.
They flood the ground with salty, acidic water.
Small geysers come and go, building cones of salt.
Next target: an island full of plants found nowhere else. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: Dallol is a hydrothermal system around a cinder cone volcano in Ethiopia's Danakil Depression, with green acid ponds below pH one. Its Afar name means dissolution or disintegration, and iron gives its ground yellow and brown colors.
